Wind and solar added 669 TWh in 2024. Total generation added 1,265.

World electricity generation, change on the year before in TWh, from Our World in Data (Ember and the Energy Institute).

Hydro, gas and coal supplied most of the other 596 TWh. Coal grew 143.

    Coal fell in 39 countries (−100 TWh) and rose in 32 (+246).

      Sources

      Our World in Data, energy dataset: the legacy owid-energy-data.csv downloaded 22 October 2026, keeping 2000 to 2024; partial 2025 is left out. The upstream revision and provider editions were not recorded.

      The electricity columns come from Ember, Yearly Electricity Data (CC BY 4.0) and, for some places and years, the Energy Institute, Statistical Review of World Energy. OWID's CC BY 4.0 covers its own contributions; third-party data retain their providers' terms. The Energy Institute's terms are its own, not CC BY: attribution is required and extensive reproduction needs its permission. Check the applicable terms before reusing this extract.

      Figures are generation, not consumption, and each is the change from the year before, so weather moves them: a wet year lifts hydro. A blank cell counts as zero only where the other sources already add up to the reported total; countries without both years are left out of the counts.
